title: workspace-ops event envelope
description: ARCHITECTURE.md §7.2, made machine-readable. This is the contract a publisher tests against; §7.2 is the prose it was derived from and remains authoritative. Both ingress doors — Redis Streams and POST /api/v1/automation/events/{code} — accept exactly this shape, and §7.1 is explicit that a behaviour on only one transport is a defect.

eventId.description: REQUIRED ON BOTH DOORS (§7.1). Identifies the OCCURRENCE, never the resource: approve → reject → approve on one record is three events with one resource id. The audited estate had 0 of 139 sends carrying one, so no consumer could tell a redelivery from a real second event. Idempotency keys on automation.event_keys, not on ingested_events (§7.4).
eventId.$comment: A publisher must pick ONE naming taxonomy before minting this. event-catalog/index.md §5: eleven call sites in the measured service insert two rows per fact under two type values, so a dual-taxonomy publisher mints two ids for one occurrence and every §7.4 guard passes.

eventType.description: <domain>.<entity>.<past-tense-verb>. Past tense is enforcement, not decoration: `customer.account.created` is a fact, `customer.account.notify_compliance` is an instruction — and an instruction in an envelope means the publisher decided something that belongs to workspace-ops. The core ships ZERO business domains; it ships five platform ones (task, process, integration, reporting, directory) because the return path re-enters through the same ingest.
eventType.$comment: The pattern cannot check tense. A reviewer must; §7.2 gives the test.

specVersion.description: The envelope version, not the publisher's.

occurredAt.description: REQUIRED. When the thing HAPPENED, not when it was received. Arrival time is the time the pipeline was healthy; under backlog the two diverge by exactly the interval where ordering matters. Several audited sends computed the real instant one line above and dropped it.
occurredAt.$comment: RFC 3339 with an explicit offset. A local timestamp with no zone is a defect an exchange operating across zones cannot absorb (§13.10).

source.description: The publishing system, e.g. `core-api`. Free text, not validated against a table.

subject.description: STRUCTURED, always both halves (ADR-29). Routing, the §7.4 cycle guard and the audit trail all key on the pair; buried in `data` it cannot be indexed and the cycle guard silently degrades to type-only.

type.description: Must be a registered automation.subject_types.code, or the envelope is `invalid`.

ref.description: OPAQUE (§7.3). Never resolved against a local table — there is no customer table and no transaction table. Only its SHAPE is checked, against subject_types.ref_format.

actor.description: Present when a HUMAN acted; null when the system did. Every audited rejection notice omitted both the rejecting reviewer and the reason, though both were persisted one line earlier.

correlationId.description: Ties one operator click, the event it produced, and every downstream effect into one thread (§12).

causationId.description: The immediate cause. Null only at the root of a thread.

depth.description: The loop guard (§7.4). Read at ingest and at emission, nowhere else. The guard keys on (eventType, subject.type, subject.ref) — not on the event type alone.

data.description: FACTS, not references. `{type, id}` requires the consumer to hold the producer's database credential and re-read a row that may have changed — a coupling that outlives every refactor. Two independent codebases in the audit converged on exactly that.
data.$comment: MONEY IS A STRING (§13.9, ADR-31). JSON numbers are IEEE-754 doubles and the domain's amounts are decimal(65,8); this is the rule that fails silently. event-catalog/index.md §4 records four production gates where a float already decides whether an event fires at all — re-reading the column as a decimal string fixes the payload and NOT the gate.

severity.description: FORBIDDEN (§7.2) — a decision, not a fact. Severity is channel_policies' to decide, per category. Rejected as `invalid`, never silently ignored.

recipients.description: FORBIDDEN (§7.2) — who is told is directory's answer, resolved from responsibility rules at dispatch. A publisher naming recipients has put routing policy back in its own codebase, which is the condition this platform exists to end.

channel.description: FORBIDDEN (§7.2) — channel_policies decides, by category × severity.

template.description: FORBIDDEN (§7.2) — templates live in the notifier driver and are not edited in this product, in either direction.

actions.description: FORBIDDEN (§7.2) — the workflow decides what happens. An envelope carrying actions is an instruction.

assignee.description: FORBIDDEN (§7.2) — task assignment is resolved, not asserted.

priority.description: FORBIDDEN (§7.2) — a decision. Note workflow priority is an integer owned by configuration, and task priority is an enum owned by the task type; neither is the publisher's.

$comment: The seven forbidden fields are declared with `not: {}` rather than left to additionalProperties so a validator names the offending field. §20·18 records that ingested_events had no column for the rejection reason and now carries `rejection jsonb {code, field, detail}` — a publisher moving off hand-rolled sends fails FIRST on these seven, and telling them which one is the whole migration aid.
